concepts.title: The Monge and Kantorovich problems
concepts.blurb:
Monge (1781) asks for a map $T$ pushing a source measure $\mu$ onto a target $
u$ at least total cost $\int c(x,T(x))\,d\mu$. The map can fail to exist (mass can't split), so Kantorovich (1942) relaxes to a coupling $\pi\in\Pi(\mu,
u)$ with marginals $\mu,
u$ minimizing $\int c\,d\pi$. The relaxed problem is a linear program: always solvable, and on the discrete side it is exactly an assignment / transportation problem.

concepts.title: Kantorovich duality
concepts.blurb:
The transport LP has a dual: maximize $\int\varphi\,d\mu+\int\psi\,d
u$ over potentials with $\varphi(x)+\psi(y)\le c(x,y)$. Strong duality holds, the optimal $\psi=\varphi^{c}$ is the $c$-transform of $\varphi$, and complementary slackness pins the support of the optimal plan to the tight set $\varphi(x)+\psi(y)=c(x,y)$. For $c(x,y)=|x-y|$ this is Kantorovich–Rubinstein: $W_1(\mu,
u)=\sup_{\mathrm{Lip}(f)\le1}\int f\,d(\mu-
u)$.

concepts.title: Wasserstein distances
concepts.blurb: The $p$-Wasserstein distance $W_p(\mu,\nu)=\big(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\int|x-y|^p\,d\pi\big)^{1/p}$ is a genuine metric on probability measures with finite $p$-th moment. It metrizes weak convergence (plus convergence of $p$-th moments), unlike total variation it sees geometry, and for two Gaussians $W_2$ has the closed form $W_2^2=|m_1-m_2|^2+(\sigma_1-\sigma_2)^2$ in one dimension.

concepts.title: Wasserstein geodesics and displacement interpolation
concepts.blurb: $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ is a geodesic space: the constant-speed geodesic from $\mu$ to $\nu$ is McCann's displacement interpolation $\mu_t=((1-t)\,\mathrm{id}+t\,T)_\#\mu$, which moves mass along straight lines rather than fading one bump out and another in. Functionals that are convex along these geodesics (displacement convexity) — entropy, potential and interaction energies — are the engine behind uniqueness and functional inequalities.

concepts.title: Otto calculus and JKO gradient flows
concepts.blurb: Otto's formal Riemannian calculus turns $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ into an infinite-dimensional manifold on which many diffusion PDEs are gradient flows of an energy. The Jordan–Kinderlehrer–Otto scheme realizes this: iterating $\mu_{k+1}=\arg\min_\rho\,\tfrac{1}{2\tau}W_2^2(\rho,\mu_k)+F(\rho)$ converges as $\tau\to0$ to the flow $\partial_t\rho=\nabla\!\cdot(\rho\nabla F'(\rho))$. For $F=$ entropy this is exactly the heat equation; adding a potential gives Fokker–Planck.
